items.title: World leaders react to Democrats' midterm sweep
items.summary: Foreign reactions on 4 Nov largely framed the US midterm results as a setback for President Trump. Spain's Pedro Sanchez welcomed the outcome, France's foreign minister called it very good news, and Norway's prime minister called it a powerful signal of a change of course. Japan stressed its alliance with Washington holds regardless.
items.why: Allies recalibrating to a divided Washington shapes trade, tariffs and the outlook for Indian exporters and multinational hiring.

items.title: Trump weighs Iran strikes or a deal after midterm loss
items.summary: Gulf News reports President Trump is weighing renewed strikes on Iran against a negotiated deal, with Vice President JD Vance urging an agreement and Qatar mediating. Brent crude fell to about $93 a barrel on hopes of diplomacy. The situation is fast-moving and details may change.
items.why: Oil prices drive India's import bill, inflation and corporate costs, so the war-or-deal call matters for budgets and hiring plans.

items.title: Regional diplomacy intensifies amid fears of a renewed US attack on Iran
items.summary: The New Arab reports Iran's foreign minister has called counterparts in Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Qatar and Oman, while Tehran's security chief met Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Iran says it sent Washington a nuclear proposal through Qatar, to be discussed only once the US meets its conditions.
items.why: Gulf stability affects remittances, energy prices and the many Indian professionals working in the region.

items.title: Moscow sceptical, Beijing measured on the US vote
items.summary: CBS News reports Russian state media suggested the results could be a blow to Ukraine, and a deputy foreign minister called the Democrats' approach to Russia extremely negative. China described the election as an internal US matter and called for a constructive strategic relationship.
items.why: Great-power positioning after the vote frames supply-chain and sanctions risk that consulting clients plan around.

items.title: Iran's speaker reads the midterms as a vote against war
items.summary: NPR's roundup of world reactions includes Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf, who wrote that Americans had said no to war. Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid used the result against Prime Minister Netanyahu, while Ukraine's government had no immediate reaction.
items.why: How rivals read US politics influences the odds of de-escalation, which feeds into markets and business sentiment.

items.title: Sensex jumps 2.6% to an eight-month high
items.summary: The Sensex closed at 79,310.01 on 5 Nov, up 2.6%, and the Nifty rose 2.4% to 24,536.60, driven by falling crude prices and foreign investor inflows. The Sensex is still about 8% below its lifetime high of December 2025.
items.why: A risk-on market eases funding conditions and tends to lift campus hiring sentiment in financial services and consulting.

items.title: Early Diwali cheer: rupee rises and bond yields ease
items.summary: Business Standard reports markets rallied on 5 Nov as the rupee strengthened and bond yields eased, linked in coverage to hopes of easing in the West Asia conflict after the US midterms.
items.why: Cheaper borrowing and a firmer rupee matter for corporate expansion plans and imported-cost pressure on margins.

items.title: PM Modi meets new NITI Aayog leadership on Viksit Bharat priorities
items.summary: Prime Minister Modi was set to meet NITI Aayog's newly appointed leadership on 5 Nov to review policy work towards the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, discuss global uncertainties and outline priorities for the 2027-28 Union Budget.
items.why: Budget priorities set the direction for public spending, skilling and employment schemes that HR and marketing teams plan against.

items.title: Cabinet backs container manufacturing and sports goods schemes; DA raised to 63%
items.summary: A governance tracker covering 16 to 31 October lists a Rs 10,000 crore Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme and a Rs 1,856.67 crore Khelo India sports goods manufacturing scheme. It also reports Dearness Allowance for central employees and pensioners rising from 60% to 63%. These are late-October decisions.
items.why: The DA hike is a pay benchmark that compensation teams watch, and manufacturing schemes signal where new jobs may appear.

items.title: AI sell-off sends the Nasdaq into correction
items.summary: NBC News reports tech stocks fell sharply on 5 Nov, with the Nasdaq 100 down 6.3% and about $2.3 trillion in market value erased, the worst day since April 2025. Investors are questioning returns on heavy AI spending, and several winning Democrats have pledged to slow AI data-centre construction. Figures are as reported on the day.
items.why: A rethink of AI spending could slow tech hiring and shift how firms justify AI-led workforce changes.

items.title: Apple slips on margin guidance; Airbnb and Palantir raise outlooks
items.summary: Yahoo Finance's earnings live blog reports Apple shares fell after its first report under new CEO John Ternus as weak margin guidance outweighed the quarter. Airbnb rose about 11% after hours on a raised full-year outlook, and Palantir beat revenue expectations and raised guidance.
items.why: Earnings season shows which business models still command investor confidence, useful context for brand and marketing strategy cases.

items.title: Canva restructures 22% of its workforce
items.summary: Canva is restructuring 22% of its workforce, affecting 1,271 employees through layoffs, role changes and moves to centralised hubs, according to a layoff tracker dated 3 Nov.
items.why: A large restructuring at a design-software leader is a live case in change management and workforce redesign, core HCOT territory.

items.title: AI-driven layoffs spread beyond tech
items.summary: Layoff trackers report job cuts linked to AI spreading into finance, logistics, consulting, media and retail, with Microsoft cutting about 4,800 roles (2.1% of staff) and Maersk trimming about 15% of corporate roles. Dates vary across the tracker entries.
items.why: Understanding where AI is replacing roles is central to workforce planning and reskilling advice in HR transformation work.

items.title: EU puts EUR 525 million into chip design start-ups
items.summary: EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen announced EUR 440 million in grants to help start-ups bring chips to market and EUR 85 million for a new European Chips Design Platform. Early-stage firms can seek up to EUR 100,000 for prototyping and advanced firms up to EUR 16 million. Sources date the announcement 4 or 5 Nov.
items.why: Public money for chip design creates specialised hiring demand and is a model for how governments compete for tech talent.

items.title: Google plans a $17 billion AI data centre; Zipline raises $1.5 billion
items.summary: A Tech Startups roundup for 5 Nov reports Google announced a $17 billion AI data centre project in Wyoming despite the sell-off, drone-delivery firm Zipline raised $1.5 billion, and Shield AI unveiled a $5.3 billion acquisition.
items.why: Big infrastructure bets alongside a market sell-off show the split view on AI that strategy and HR leaders must plan through.

items.title: Hundreds of thousands of Nvidia H200 chips wait in Hong Kong
items.summary: About 600,000 Nvidia H200 AI chips are reportedly sitting in Hong Kong as Chinese authorities continue to withhold permission for large-scale imports into the mainland, according to coverage on 5 Nov. The figure is a reported estimate.
items.why: Chip trade frictions affect the cost and pace of AI adoption, which shapes how quickly firms automate roles.

items.title: Winning Democrats pledge to slow AI data-centre construction
items.summary: NBC News reports numerous Democrats who won governor, attorney general, Senate and House races pledged to slow or halt construction of AI data centres, adding a political risk to the AI build-out.
items.why: Regulation of AI infrastructure could change where tech jobs and investment land, a factor in location and workforce strategy.

items.title: the Nasdaq 100 lost about $2.3 trillion in one day
items.summary: NBC News reports the 6.3% drop on 5 Nov erased roughly $2.3 trillion in market value, the index's worst day since April 2025.

items.title: the Sensex is about 8% below its record
items.summary: After the 5 Nov rally the Sensex sits roughly 7.95% below its lifetime high of 86,159.02, set on 1 December 2025.

items.title: EU chip grants go up to EUR 16 million per firm
items.summary: Under the new EU scheme, early-stage start-ups can seek up to EUR 100,000 for prototyping and more advanced firms up to EUR 16 million.
